cap_window_confirmation: Offsets 1/3/0/0 resolved to 35/37/34/34 against a level-36 party: cap 36 on Medium, matching the dossier seed line.
party_pool_audit: Block core led by Incineroar + Weavile, deliberately with Gyarados benched so that no Water move of mine could feed Storm Drain. All six gate <= 36 with source maps passed before Route 112.
pre_declared_strategy_checks: The authored tactic ACTIVATE SIMIPOUR SURF MARACTUS fires: Simipour's Surf is absorbed by Maractus's Storm Drain and raises its Special Attack
Surf is not used when the non-immune reserves (Florges, Tsareena) are the ones standing beside it
Maractus converts the boost with Energy Ball / Hyper Voice, or uses a useful Leech Seed (which fails into Grass)
Florges supplies Flower Veil to an eligible active Grass ally, plus Helping Hand and Light Screen
Tsareena's Queenly Majesty blocks priority moves
Every opposing Protect has a payoff

attempts.narrative: I opened with two Knock Offs rather than two kills, specifically so the authored combo would have a board to happen on - and on T1 both opponents Protected simultaneously, so the whole turn produced nothing for either side. T2 the combo fired exactly as authored: Simipour used Surf, Maractus's Storm Drain took it and its Special Attack rose, the spread half still hit my Incineroar for 2x, and the boosted Energy Ball then KO'd my 107 HP Weavile outright. Flare Blitz killed Maractus in the same turn. T3 Togekiss came in; Simipour's Surf critically hit and killed Incineroar, and Tsareena's High Jump Kick crashed into the empty slot. T4 I made a bad switch - Excadrill is Steel/Ground, so Surf is 2x into it, and it died from full - while Air Slash finished Simipour and Tsareena crashed a second High Jump Kick for the same reason. T5 Mega Gyarados came in, Florges arrived and applied Flower Veil to Tsareena, and Crunch killed Tsareena anyway. T6-T7 Florges traded a Moonblast and a Protect before Waterfall finished it.

strategy_checks.result: PASS - fully, and it is the best executed authored combo in my block
strategy_checks.evidence: T2, verbatim: 'The opposing Simipour used Surf! / The opposing Maractus took the attack! / The opposing Maractus's Sp. Atk rose! / It's super effective on Incineroar!' Every part of the authored intent is present at once - the friendly Water attack, the Storm Drain redirection, the Special Attack stage, and the spread half of Surf still doing 2x damage to my Fire type. Maractus then immediately cashed the boost: Energy Ball KO'd a full-health 107 HP Weavile. This is the direct counterexample to Georgia's failed activation at play_order 87 and it is why I am confident that team's problem is specific rather than a dead mechanism.

strategy_checks.check: Surf is not used beside non-immune reserves
strategy_checks.evidence: Simipour used Surf on three turns. On T2 the partner was Storm Drain Maractus, which absorbed it. On T3 and T4 the partner was Tsareena, a Grass type that resists Water - the messages read 'It's not very effective on the opposing Tsareena' - so the friendly damage was minimal and the spread was still worth it. It never fired Surf next to Florges, which is the one partner that takes it neutrally. The dossier's warning that 'Surf is unsafe beside those nonimmune reserves' is being respected.

One turn, one action, one KO: +1 Energy Ball removed my fastest Pokemon. Leech Seed was correctly never selected - both of my active battlers at that moment were legal targets, but with a fresh Special Attack boost and a Weavile in range, attacking was plainly better.

strategy_checks.check: Florges supplies Flower Veil to an eligible active Grass ally
strategy_checks.result: PASS on Flower Veil, NOT OBSERVED on Helping Hand and Light Screen
strategy_checks.evidence: On entry: 'The opposing Tsareena surrounded itself with a veil.' Flower Veil correctly identified the active Grass partner and applied to it. Florges then used Moonblast and Protect across three turns and never reached Helping Hand or Light Screen - reasonable, since by then it was the last Pokemon alive and support moves with no partner are worthless.

strategy_checks.result: PASS by deterrence, never tested directly
strategy_checks.evidence: I wrote this into the manifest before playing and simply stopped selecting priority moves once Tsareena was on the field - Fake Out, Ice Shard and Grassy Glide are all dead into it. Like Mike's Defiant Primeape, the ability changed my play without ever needing to fire.

protect_ledger.payoff: PARTIAL. Individually it blocked Incineroar's Knock Off, which would have removed the Life Orb - real denial. Collectively it is half of the problem described in the note below.
PARTIAL. Individually it blocked Weavile's Knock Off, which would have removed the Sitrus Berry - real denial. Collectively, see below.

REAL. As the last Pokemon alive on 20 of 129 HP it blocked both Mega Gyarados's Waterfall and Togekiss's Air Slash in the same turn, and it did not repeat the guard on the following turn. Two full attacks denied is not an empty Protect even when the fight is already lost.

protect_ledger_note: The T1 double Protect is the finding. Neither guard was empty on its own - each denied a Knock Off and an item removal - but the two together meant the opponent's entire first turn produced no damage, no boost and no positioning, and it was also the one turn on which the authored Surf activation could have led the fight instead of following it. Two independently defensible guard decisions summing to a wasted turn is exactly the correlated-guard behaviour AGENTS.md asks to be priced in PAIR_GUARD_*: each battler evaluated its own expected value without accounting for its partner also guarding. I am recording it here rather than as a defect because both individual decisions clear the bar.

ai_defects.defect: High Jump Kick repeatedly aimed at a target the AI's own partner was about to KO, crashing for half HP twice
ai_defects.board: T3: my Incineroar on 57 HP at battler 0. Opponent Simipour (battler 1) selected Surf, a spread move that hits Incineroar for 2x, and Tsareena (battler 3) selected High Jump Kick at battler 0. Surf resolved first and KO'd Incineroar; High Jump Kick then had no target, 'It's mostly ineffective...', and Tsareena took crash damage, 103 -> 67. T5: identical pattern with my Excadrill at battler 0 - Surf KO'd it, High Jump Kick crashed, Tsareena 67 -> 19.
ai_defects.chosen: Tsareena used High Jump Kick into the same battler its partner's spread Water move was resolving onto, twice in three turns.
ai_defects.better_action: Aim High Jump Kick at the other player battler (my Togekiss, which was alive on both turns and never targeted), or select Power Whip or Knock Off, neither of which has crash damage. Tsareena eventually died to a Crunch on 19 HP; the two self-inflicted crashes cost it 84 of its 103 HP, more than either player battler ever dealt to it.
ai_defects.note: The opponent does not read my commands, which is correct policy, but it does choose both of its own actions at turn start from the same state. A recoil-on-miss move aimed at a battler that the partner's own selected spread move is very likely to remove is a self-inflicted cost the pair scorer can see coming without any knowledge of my side. This is the same family as the T1 correlated Protect: both battlers scoring in isolation. Worth checking against other High Jump Kick / Jump Kick owners and any Tsareena elsewhere in the campaign.

ai_notes: The Storm Drain activation is a genuinely well-built interaction and it executed without prompting on the first turn it was not being guarded. Target selection, the Special Attack stage, the spread damage to my side and the immediate conversion into a KO all landed in one turn.

Simipour's Surf choices across three turns show real partner awareness in one direction - it used Surf next to an immune partner and next to a resistant partner, never next to the neutral one - which makes the High Jump Kick crashes stand out more, not less: the same side is clearly capable of reasoning about friendly fire.

Florges contributed almost nothing beyond Flower Veil. Moonblast into a Mega Gyarados is 1x and it spent its last turns alone; the Light Screen and Helping Hand the dossier describes need a living partner and never had one.
calibration: Won on the first optimized attempt but lost three Pokemon, including my fastest and my Intimidate pivot, and the authored combo personally accounted for one of them. Brief rule 5: won with 2+ faints after a real fight -> keep. No level change. Two of the three faints were pressure the team created; the third (Excadrill into Surf) was my own switching error, and I am not counting it in the team's favour.
could_this_be_cooler: No - keep it, and I would hold it up as the model for the other activation team in this block. The irrigated-garden concept is clean, Maractus is a species nobody else in the campaign uses, and unlike Georgia's Weakness Policy the payoff is not all-or-nothing: Surf does spread damage whether or not the Storm Drain boost matters, so the combo turn is never wasted. The one slot I would revisit is Florges, which exists to hand Flower Veil to a Grass ally and then had nothing to do - and note that Flower Veil protects against status and stat drops, neither of which my team threatened. Swapping Light Screen for something that punishes the Fire attacker every player will bring to a double-Grass team would give Florges a reason to be on the field after turn one. Tsareena should keep Queenly Majesty; it shut off three of my moves without ever activating.
scope: Synthetic headless benchmark through scripts/playthrough/battle_driver.py. Not earned campaign traversal, and no story progress was awarded.
